Disabled.test-tls13-ecdsa-support.py: SCOPE — 5 of 10 over the ecdsa leaf, its best. Three failures are brainpool curves (DESIGN.md §1); the other two ask the server to sign with ecdsa_secp384r1_sha384 and ecdsa_secp521r1_sha512, which need a P-384 and a P-521 leaf, and src/testdata ships neither. Disabled.test-tls13-finished.py: KEEP — 39 of 42 over the rsa leaf; real OpenSSL passes 42. All three remaining send a Finished whose body is not the negotiated hash's length and want decode_error for it (§6.2, "the length of the message was incorrect"); zssl answers decrypt_error, which is what §4.4.4 demands of a Finished whose "contents are correct" test fails, and what BoGo's TrailingMessageData-TLS13-*Finished cases require of us in as many words. The two corpora disagree here and both run against this tree; finding 7 in docs/TLSFUZZER.md records the split and why §4.4.4 wins.
Disabled.test-tls13-keyupdate-from-server.py: Not a defect — 2 of 3 over the rsa leaf. The one failure needs a server that sends a post-handshake KeyUpdate when the client fetches /keyupdate; this harness echoes rather than serving resources, and real OpenSSL s_server fails the same conversation.
Disabled.test-tls13-keyupdate.py: Not a defect — 58 to 60 of 62 over the rsa leaf; the script samples its own vectors, so which conversations remain moves run to run. Finding 7 in docs/TLSFUZZER.md closed the two length cases ('empty' and 'large KeyUpdate message', now decode_error). What is left is finding 10, the harness echoing each application-data record where the script sends a request in several and waits for one reply. Real OpenSSL passes 62.
Disabled.test-tls13-large-number-of-extensions.py: Not a defect — 2 of 22 over the rsa leaf, and real OpenSSL scores exactly the same 2 of 22. The script offers ClientHellos carrying a thousand-odd extensions; zssl caps them at 64 (client_hello.zig extensions_count_max) and answers decode_error. That is a deliberate bound under the no-allocator budget, and the corpus does not agree with itself about it.
Disabled.test-tls13-legacy-version.py: OPEN GAP — 2 of 10 over either leaf; real OpenSSL passes 9. zssl ignores ClientHello.legacy_version once supported_versions is present, which is what §4.2.1 requires of *negotiation*; the script and OpenSSL both refuse implausible values outright with protocol_version. Finding 11 in docs/TLSFUZZER.md argues it both ways.
Disabled.test-tls13-mldsa-in-certificate-verify.p: Client certificates: out of scope permanently (DESIGN.md §1).
Disabled.test-tls13-mlkem.py: ML-KEM: post-quantum key exchange, not implemented (DESIGN.md §1).
Disabled.test-tls13-multiple-ccs-messages.py: Not a defect — 4 of 7 over either leaf, and real OpenSSL 3.6.3 scores 2 of 7, failing even the script's own 'sanity with one CCS message'. Finding 8 in docs/TLSFUZZER.md closed 'multiple CCS Messages in one TLS record', which was a payload we never read — OpenSSL still fails that one, so we are stricter than it is on §5's MUST. The three that remain ask for unexpected_message on a *second* compatibility CCS; §5 caps neither the count nor the placement inside its window, and zssl's own bound is two (ServerHandshake ccs_seen_max), which a HelloRetryRequest flight needs.
Disabled.test-tls13-non-support.py: TLS 1.2: the script expects a ServerHello at (3,3) followed by a ServerHelloDone, so every conversation asks for a version zssl does not implement (DESIGN.md §1).
Disabled.test-tls13-post-handshake-auth.py: Client certificates: out of scope permanently (DESIGN.md §1).
Disabled.test-tls13-psk_dhe_ke.py: SCOPE — 0 of 4 over either leaf, and real OpenSSL also scores 0 of 4 with no PSK configured. Every conversation offers an *external* PSK, and zssl has none: §4.2.11.2 derives binder_key under "ext binder" for an externally established PSK and "res binder" for a resumption one, and key_schedule.zig only ever writes "res binder" — so an external binder cannot verify and we answer decrypt_error. DESIGN.md §1 scopes this to "PSK resumption" and Config.psk_lookup calls itself the resumption seam, so the capability was never claimed. Finding 12 in docs/TLSFUZZER.md has the measurement; harness flags alone do not reach it.
Disabled.test-tls13-psk_ke.py: psk_ke without (EC)DHE is never accepted (DESIGN.md §6, slice 3).
Disabled.test-tls13-rsapss-signatures.py: SCOPE — 3 of 8 over the ecdsa leaf, 0 of 8 over the rsa one. The script's own sanity offers rsa_pss_pss_* alone, which needs a certificate holding an id-RSASSA-PSS key; src/testdata's RSA leaf is rsaEncryption and can answer only rsa_pss_rsae_*. Its --rsa flag does not help, because sanity still asks for pss.
Disabled.test-tls13-serverhello-random.py: SCOPE — 128 of 256 over the rsa leaf, and every one of the 128 failures is 'TLS 1.3 with ffdhe2048'. Finite-field DHE is out of scope (DESIGN.md §1); the x25519 half of the sweep passes.
Disabled.test-tls13-session-resumption.py: SCOPE — 4 of 7 over the rsa leaf, and real OpenSSL fails the identical 3. Two are TLS 1.2 conversations; the third is PSK_ONLY, which is psk_ke without (EC)DHE and never accepted (DESIGN.md §6, slice 3) — a client offering only psk_ke is issued no ticket, which is what the script's mandatory ExpectNewSessionTicket trips on.
Disabled.test-tls13-shuffled-extentions.py: Not a defect — 2 of 19 over the rsa leaf, and real OpenSSL fails the identical 17. Sixteen of them put 4096 unassigned extensions in the first hello, past zssl's cap of 64. The seventeenth wants illegal_parameter when the second, post-HelloRetryRequest hello reorders its extension block; §4.1.2 asks for the same ClientHello but does not call reordering a modification, and neither implementation here enforces it.
Disabled.test-tls13-signature-algorithms.py: SCOPE — 95 of 102 over the rsa leaf; real OpenSSL passes 102. Five are hellos advertising 213 to 32715 signature schemes, past zssl's cap of 64 (client_hello.zig schemes_count_max), the same deliberate bound as the extension cap. The rest push a ClientHello past the embedder's reassembly buffer, which is a capacity refusal and says so: unlike a Finished or a KeyUpdate, a hello has no length its type fixes, so finding 7 has nothing to decide it on.
Disabled.test-tls13-symetric-ciphers.py: AES-CCM: every failure is TLS_AES_128_CCM_SHA256 or TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256, outside the suite policy (DESIGN.md §1). No count here on purpose — the script randomises its fuzz vectors, so it varies run to run.
Disabled.test-tls13-version-negotiation.py: TLS 1.2: every failing conversation is a fallback from a 1.3 draft codepoint to 1.2, which zssl does not implement (DESIGN.md §1).
Disabled.test-tls13-zero-content-type.py: Not a defect — 6 of 8 over either leaf; real OpenSSL passes 8. Both failures are finding 10 in docs/TLSFUZZER.md: the harness echoes each application-data record, and these two conversations send a request in three records and wait for a single reply.
Disabled.test-tls13-zero-length-data.py: Not a defect — 8 of 11 over the rsa leaf; real OpenSSL passes 11. All three failures are finding 10, the harness's per-record echo answering a three-record request three times.
